work_item.role: W1 public-evidence discovery and neutral admission

discovery_pass.method: Direction-blind discovery and admission of a public repeated same-model cross-harness benchmark with committed raw-run tuples, runner scripts, task identity, objective test gate, and immutable repository revision.
discovery_pass.hardware: single NVIDIA DGX Spark GB10 SM121, 128 GiB unified memory
discovery_pass.reasoning_policy: thinking:false / reasoning none forced by source benchmark
discovery_pass.evaluator: objective pytest gate over tests/hermes_state/test_reasoning_roundtrip.py and tests/cli/test_branch_command.py
discovery_pass.reset_policy: fresh workdir extracted from immutable task tarball for each run; per-run metering log reset

protocol_deviations_and_failures.detail: The source names each harness but does not publish the exact CLI/package versions used in the benchmark runs.
The committed runner/Dockerfile contains a truncated FROM line and does not recover exact installed package versions. W1 does not infer them from current releases.

Hermes is run natively on the DGX Spark while the other four harnesses run in the runner container. The same model server, metering proxy, immutable task tarball, timeout, task prompt, and objective test gate are retained, but execution-surface equivalence is not assumed.
Five repetitions are available per harness, but all repetitions target one cross-module software bug. W1 makes no generalization beyond the published surface.

non_admission_dispositions.reason: The current AWS sample tree documents a multi-harness runner, but its commit history explicitly says the per-harness result reports from the earlier source fork were not imported. Existing source-fork observations are reused elsewhere rather than duplicated from documentation-only AWS surfaces.
The source benchmark excludes Aider because its tested pair-programming workflow would require human staging of files, so no result is invented or reconstructed.

non_admission_dispositions.surface: publisher interpretive headline and harness ordering
non_admission_dispositions.reason: W1 preserves factual pass counts and token aggregates without adopting the source's evaluative interpretation or declaring a preferred harness.
